---
title: "Data & methods"
---

## Data source

This project uses public individual-level files from the **2017–2018 National
Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)**, conducted by the U.S.
National Center for Health Statistics:

- [NHANES 2017–2018 survey documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/continuousnhanes/default.aspx?BeginYear=2017)
- [Physical Activity Questionnaire (PAQ_J)](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/PAQ_J.htm)
- [Depression Screener (DPQ_J)](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/DPQ_J.htm)
- [Demographics (DEMO_J)](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/DEMO_J.htm)

The source files used for this reproducible site are included in the
[`data/`](data/) folder. Respondents are linked across files using the
NHANES sequence number (`SEQN`).

## Measures

- **Depressive symptoms:** The nine DPQ items are added to form a PHQ-9 score
  from 0 to 27. The score is a screening measure, not a diagnosis. Records
  missing any of the nine answers are excluded from the plots.
- **Recreational activity:** Minutes per week are calculated as reported
  minutes per day multiplied by reported days per week for vigorous and
  moderate recreational activities, then summed. A reported “no” is counted
  as zero for that activity; refused, unknown, and incomplete responses are
  treated as missing. Work and transportation activity are not included.
- **Demographic panels:** The charts use the male/female categories recorded
  in the NHANES `RIAGENDR` field. They do not represent every aspect of sex or
  gender.
- **Included sample:** Adults with complete depression, activity, and
  demographic values are included. The homepage reports the resulting count
  directly from the analysis code.

## Important limitations

The figures are descriptive and use complete cases without applying NHANES
survey weights. They should not be read as official population estimates.
The survey is observational and these plots do not show that activity causes
changes in depressive symptoms. The leisure-time activity measure is only one
part of physical activity, and other factors may be associated with both
activity and mood.

The original proposal considered NCAA athletes and wrestling. The NCAA study
page reports about 23,000 participants, but the individual-level records needed
to plot thousands of actual responses were not available here. This website
therefore uses a public dataset that does support a real observation-level
graphic; its results are about U.S. adults, not student-athletes.
